pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Denmark Road High School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
A very warm welcome to the Denmark Road High School website.
So, I have been set the impossible task of describing our school to you in written word. When you visit our school you will understand my predicament. The feeling is something you simply have to experience, words cannot portray who and what we actually are. On behalf of our community I extend a warm welcome to you all, please come to our Open Mornings and Evenings or contact us on 01452 543335 or reception@denmarkroad.org to arrange a visit.
What I can explain is what we believe in and stand for. We understand we are preparing your daughters and sons to embrace more opportunities and face more complex challenges than ever before. They are our future leaders; our next generation of doctors, lawyers and entrepreneurs. It is an amazing responsibility which rests on their shoulders. We, in turn, recognise and embrace our duty and privilege in preparing them for this.
We belong. We are a beacon for curiosity, determination, respect and reflection.
At Denmark Road High School, we live our values every day.
We foster a culture of Respect. We respect ourselves, one another, our school, humankind and the environment. Relationships are at the heart of everything we do because it is through kindness, inclusion and understanding that people flourish. We celebrate our diverse communities and encourage every individual to feel safe, valued and proud to be themselves.
We nurture Curiosity. We want our young people to learn about themselves and the world around them so that they can make a positive difference. We create opportunities for intellectual exploration, creativity, enrichment and leadership, helping students develop a genuine joy in learning and the confidence to embrace new experiences.
We value Reflection. We encourage our community to think deeply about their motivations, actions and impact. Through reflection, we develop self-awareness, empathy and the wisdom to grow as learners, leaders and citizens.
We inspire Determination. We encourage our students and staff to embrace challenge, pursue their ambitions and persevere. Through memorable experiences within and beyond the classroom, we help young people develop the confidence and aspiration needed to thrive personally, socially and academically, both now and in the future.
At the core of our success is our commitment to people. We prioritise wellbeing, professional fulfilment and collaboration, enabling our staff and students alike to develop, and feel safe to be, themselves. We nurture each individual through a balance of deep human understanding and thoughtful innovation, empowering our young people to navigate the future with purpose.
Denmark Road High School is consistently ranked amongst the highest-performing state schools in the country. However, our success is not built upon outcomes alone. It is built upon the strength of our community, the quality of our relationships, and our unwavering commitment to the whole child. We know that when people feel they belong, they achieve remarkable things.
Our school is remarkable.
Please come and see it for yourself.
Miss Claire Giblin Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: School Vision & Ethos - Denmark Road High School
pageCache.text:
School Vision & Ethos
Respect, Curiosity, Reflection, Determination,
We respect ourselves, our school, humankind, and the environment.
We are curious to learn more about ourselves and the world around us in order to make a positive difference.
We reflect to better understand our motivations, actions and inactions, and their impacts.
We are determined in our attitude towards life and learning.
Vision 2030
We belong. We are a beacon for curiosity, determination, respect, and reflection.
We belong. We are beacons for curiosity, determination, respect, and reflection.
We thrive in a culture of kindness and shared responsibility. Denmark Road enables all of us to learn about, and feel safe to be, ourselves. We celebrate our communities and experience diverse perspectives that grow our view of the world. We have the space to be imaginative, and we experience joy in our learning. Ambition is encouraged and valued: we develop our ideas, pursue interests, and try new things that help us to thrive personally, socially and academically now, and in our futures.
We belong. We champion curiosity, determination, respect, and reflection.
We are advocates for intellectual exploration, enrichment, extra-curricular opportunity, and leadership. As the school of choice, we are known for prioritising staff wellbeing, professional fulfilment and collaboration. Denmark Road enables all of us to develop, and feel safe to be, ourselves.
We nurture the development of each individual, balancing deep human understanding alongside the thoughtful and innovative integration of technology, to empower our young people to navigate the future with purpose. We lead with integrity and build local and international pathways, transforming practises in the wider educational community.
We belong. We are proud to support our students, staff and school in their curiosity, determination, respect and reflection.
We celebrate our connection to the school, both past, present, and future. We embrace our role in the school community, contributing to a diverse culture of pride and shared responsibility, empowering our young people to thrive now and in the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama - Subjects - Denmark Road High School
pageCache.text:
Drama
Drama at Denmark Road offers the chance for students to challenge themselves to develop a range of practical and personal skills. Across Key Stage 3 and 4, students must work independently and collaboratively to react to, and understand, stimuli and scripts and make creative choices in their interpretations. We are proud of the pressure this puts students under. In all drama lessons we seek to explore and expose how theatre can be performed to entertain, question, to challenge and to express complex ideas around society, politics and humanity.
Welcome
Drama at Denmark Road has grown massively over the last five years, from teaching GCSE for the first time in 2020, to moving into a brilliant new space and launching A Level in September 2026. In every lesson, students develop and refine real-world skills of communication, collaboration, creativity, independence, organisation and many more.
Curriculum
We work with students twice a fortnight at KS3 and offer the subject as option at GCSE and A Level. We begin Year 7 assuming no prior study of the subject and focus on developing a range of skills: from working responsibly and safely, to physical and vocal communication, staging, directing, design skills and written evaluation. Students study a range of engaging and challenging set texts including the full texts ‘A Monster Calls’ and ‘DNA’. We foster close ties with the English Department and use content from texts already tackled by students including ‘A Christmas Carol’, ‘Medusa’, ‘Macbeth’ and more meaning we can focus and hone skills in performance, design and reflection- essential to anyone interested in succeeding in the subject.
At GCSE we study the Eduqas specification - for more information on the outline of the course click here. We currently have over 70 students studying Drama in Years 10 and 11. At A Level we follow the Edexcel Drama and Theatre with set texts Equus and Lysistrata.
Extra Curricular
We’re very proud of the hard work that goes into extra curricular Drama at DRHS. We currently produce KS4 and KS5 Drama in February each year- you can watch previous trailers here for ‘Find Me’ (Feb, 2025) and ‘Anti-Hero’ (Feb, 2026). We also collaborate extensively with the Music department to produce a whole-school musical in Term 6. This year it will be ‘Into the Woods’. Recently we’ve produced ‘Legally Blonde’ and ‘Matilda’ as whole-school shows.
We take students on multiple theatre trips every year to watch live shows from internationally renowned directors and companies including Frantic Assembly, Emma Rice, The RSC, Complicite, Splendid and many more.
For more information on the department please contact Mr Fitch, Subject Leader for Drama and Media Marketing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Design - Subjects - Denmark Road High School
pageCache.text:
Art & Design
The purpose of our Art & Design curriculum is to allow students to develop a keen interest of a subject that is both intellectually engaging and creatively demanding, our mission being to make this appreciation for the arts accessible for all. We aim to achieve this through a progressive curriculum which celebrates the importance of inclusivity and representation through a wide diversity of artists, movements and cultures, exploring how these evolve over time.
Our long-term curriculum is structured so that key artistic skills, materials, processes and techniques are embedded and sequentially built upon throughout KS3 providing students with a strong foundation to build upon. These skills are taught through a combination of practical activities in a broad range of art mediums, such as drawing, painting, textiles and three-dimensional design, in conjunction with theoretical studies, the goal being to nurture creativity, critical thinking and a well-rounded understanding of the visual arts.
We are aware that art education contributes to the development of well-rounded individuals by allowing them to hone fundamental life skills that go beyond the classroom. We encourage our students to explore and expand their analytical and problem-solving skills, to take risks and approach challenges with tenacity and innovative solutions. We ensure students feel comfortable to challenge preconceived ideas, form their own opinions and be able to effectively communicate these through their work. Our intent is to cultivate creativity, broaden perspectives and enrich individual characters.

pageCache.pageTitle: Biology - Subjects - Denmark Road High School
pageCache.text:
Biology
We produce inquisitive, confident scientists who appreciate the history of biological discovery and have a life-long love of biology and the natural world.
We want our students to have a secure understanding of core biological concepts and to be able to correctly sequence and describe biological processes which are essential to life and relate to all living organisms; to understand the purpose and principles of practical work and have developed their experimental skills and strategies, analytical, evaluative and observational skills as well as their scientific reasoning; to also have well-developed scientific literacy and oracy and have a secure knowledge of biological vocabulary, terminology and definitions and be able to explain their ideas clearly, both written and verbally, based on scientific evidence.
We want to will inspire and motivate our students to aspire to rewarding and exciting biology-based careers and be part of the drive towards solving our many global challenges; climate change, tackling the reduction of biodiversity, the impact of human and animal disease and the ethics of modern gene technologies.

pageCache.pageTitle: History - Subjects - Denmark Road High School
pageCache.text:
History
The History curriculum is designed in a chronological way with common ‘drivers’ of history being embedded throughout. Some of these being power, religion and the role of women. Within this, we challenge students to think about how events of the past can be linked together. To develop this, the use of Big Questions helps bring students learning together. Topics have been chosen to not only understand why the world is the way it is, but also be reflective of our community and discover students' own history. This is why we look to explore History on a local, national and global scale. Looking from different perspectives to see History from the ‘top down’ but also ‘bottom up’. Central to this is the development of core historical skills. Students learn to use second order concepts, work with primary sources and historians’ interpretations to think critically and challenge the narrative.

pageCache.text:
Careers Programme & Work Experience
At Denmark Road High School, we aim to support students, so that they can make informed decisions about their future, by raising aspirations, offering and promoting varied opportunities and providing impartial and independent information and guidance.
DRHS is committed to providing all students in Years 7-13 with a Careers Programme that has been developed in line with the eight Gatsby benchmarks for ensuring best practice and to meet the requirements of the Department for Education’s statutory guidance.
Our Careers Lead is Mrs Lindsay Harvey.
Contact our Careers Lead
The Careers programme at DRHS has been planned across Years 7 – 13 to support students in gaining the skills and knowledge they need to make informed decisions about their future.
The core programme is delivered through the Careers in Tutorial Programme. This programme has been specifically arranged to enable progression and development, through the use of Unifrog, from Years 7 and 13 and to meet the Gatsby benchmarks. Each student has their own account.
7-13 Careers in Tutorial Programme
Online Resources for Students, Parents and Carers
At DRHS we work with independent and highly qualified Careers Advisors who carry out at least one 1:1 30 to 40-minute career interview with all students in both KS4 and KS5.
Additionally, students can choose to purchase life-long access to Morrisby, an online careers platform and this is funded by the school for students eligible for support through Pupil Premium or Forces Premium. Our Careers Advisors are fully trained Morrisby Advisors.
Unifrog is a fully comprehensive, impartial careers platform that allows students to become further immersed in learning about their future options. It is used as a key tool in the delivery of Careers.
Every student has their own account which they can access at any time from any device. The tools, activities and opportunities presented by Unifrog are supported by Form Tutors. This helps students to chart skill development and allows them to reflect on the opportunities they have both at home and at school to personally develop.
Parents and carers are welcome to create their own parent account where they’ll be able to see what their child is doing on Unifrog, including any interactions tagged against their name and any upcoming events we’ve logged for them. They’ll also be able to use all the same tools their child can to support them on their Unifrog journey. To read more about Unifrog for Parents please click here.
In addition, there are other events and activities that are planned alongside the Tutorial programme to support Careers at DRHS. For example:
STEM INVEST days, competitions and activities
Arts INVEST days, workshops and visiting artists
Maths Inspiration
Unifrog Overview
We think it is very important that students (and parents) have access to a wide range of information about different careers and also the labour market.
Careers related information and guidance specifically relates to careers, jobs and training. At DRHS this includes advice and guidance on choices and options at KS4, Post-16 and Post- 18 – for example applying for an apprenticeship, taking a gap year or going to university in the UK or abroad.
Labour market information is about current work and job/apprenticeship opportunities in specific locations. This includes information about companies and organisations, industries, occupations and professions. It also includes information on the labour market in terms of past and present trends as well as future demands which can be useful for students thinking about post-university opportunities.
There are a wide range of sources for this information and it is an area that changes regularly.
Some sources of information are included in our careers programme, such as Unifrog and UCAS.
Throughout the year, the school is made aware of new and current opportunities that relate to careers that are not part of the planned programme.
Many of these are sent to the school by email and so we are not always able to verify the quality of the offer. However, we do our best to find out if other schools are aware of them or if they are from known providers. In most cases, we then pass the details on to parents and students.
Throughout the year, students are asked to reflect on their progress within careers through Unifrog. This helps students to chart skill development and allows them to reflect on the opportunities they have had to personally develop.

Our Careers programme is reviewed annually using the Compass Tool to ensure that our provision meets the Gatsby benchmarks.
We work with the Gloucestershire Learning and Enterprise Partnership, LEP who have access to the Compass Tool results and are able to support schools in moving forward with careers.
